html:
One Hundred Years of Solitude is a novel by the Colombian writer Gabriel García Márquez, published in Buenos Aires in 1967. It is the best known work of magic realism and of the Latin American Boom.

It follows seven generations of the Buendía family in Macondo, an imaginary town in the swamps of Colombia, from its founding to its end. Ghosts, a plague of insomnia, a rain of yellow flowers and a woman who rises to heaven are told in the same calm voice as weddings and wars. Names repeat across the generations, and so do the family's mistakes.

The story also follows real Colombian history: the civil wars between Liberals and Conservatives, and the coming of a foreign banana company. Its massacre of striking workers is based on the banana massacre of 1928.

The book was an immediate success in the Spanish speaking world, then everywhere. It has been translated into dozens of languages and has sold tens of millions of copies. It helped win its author the Nobel Prize in 1982.
sum: One Hundred Years of Solitude is a novel by the Colombian writer Gabriel García Márquez, published in Buenos Aires in 1967. It is the best known work of magic realism and of the Latin American Boom.
